tasks.title: Establish the consumer UI design system and application shell
tasks.summary: Create the shared tokens, layout, navigation, surfaces, controls, chips, banners, cards, disclosures, empty states, and responsive/accessibility foundations required by every redesigned workflow.
tasks.objective: Replace raw browser-form presentation with one restrained, reusable visual and interaction system before screen-specific work begins.
tasks.context: The current application has inconsistent spacing, weak grouping, competing actions, and screen-local CSS. Later UX tasks must consume stable shared primitives instead of introducing parallel styling systems.
inputs: Existing Vue shell and accessible shared primitives
outputs: Design tokens and global layout rules
implementation_notes: Use a small 4/8-based spacing system, deliberate content widths, clear typography hierarchy, subtle surfaces, consistent radii/borders, and restrained shadows.
Provide visible hover/focus/pressed/disabled states and comfortable interaction targets without relying on color alone.
Keep primary navigation Ranked feed, Library, Sources, and Settings; preserve the local-only indicator with clearer treatment.
Create primitives generic enough for later screens, but do not rewrite feature workflows in this task.
Do not add a remote CSS framework, analytics, fonts, runtime CDN assets, or a second client-state architecture.
acceptance_criteria: The application shell has clear hierarchy and a consistent bounded content area at desktop and approximately 390px without horizontal overflow.
Shared fields, buttons, chips, cards, banners, disclosures, action groups, and empty states expose semantic markup, visible focus, and consistent spacing.
Primary, secondary, and tertiary actions are visually distinguishable and meet keyboard/touch usability expectations.
Existing routes, local-only status, API error announcements, and accessibility semantics continue to work.
Later feature tasks can compose the primitives without adding competing global design rules.
verification: Run frontend lint, typecheck, shared-component tests, and production build.
Add keyboard and automated accessibility coverage for navigation and all new interactive primitives.
Render representative shell/primitive states at desktop and approximately 390px and assert no horizontal overflow.
Inspect screenshots for spacing rhythm, grouping, contrast, focus, action priority, and consistency.
tasks.handoff_notes: UX-002, UX-003, and UX-004 must use these accepted primitives and must not independently redefine the global visual system.

tasks.title: Redesign onboarding and personalization settings
tasks.summary: Replace the giant technical profile form with four-step onboarding, accessible interest chips, human-facing optional location, secondary demographics, reorganized Settings, and semantic ranking controls.
tasks.objective: Let an ordinary user configure interests, Budapest/Hungary, starter sources, and ranking style without understanding administrative schemas or numeric ranking mathematics.
tasks.context: Existing APIs and SQLite representations are accepted. Adapt cleanly to them unless an unavoidable contract gap is proven and handed back before implementation.
inputs: Existing persisted profile and RankingConfiguration behavior
implementation_notes: Use Interests, optional Location, Sources, and Finish as clearly separated onboarding steps with one final primary action.
Give new interests the existing canonical default weight and preserve saved per-interest weights; any precise editing is advanced-only.

Present Country using human-readable values and City or area as the normal locality input. Map Budapest/Hungary safely onto the existing country/region/city contract; keep unusual administrative detail advanced-only if needed.
Keep age/gender collapsed by default with explicit publisher-audience explanations and clear neutral disablement.

Map Balanced, More personalized, More recent, and any advanced semantic controls deterministically to accepted weights/caps. Existing non-preset configurations must remain representable as custom/advanced without silent overwrite.
Do not add geolocation, remote lookup, inference, or browser-authoritative profile state.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can add/remove example and custom interest chips, choose starter sources, enter Hungary and Budapest, skip optional demographics, and finish setup without seeing raw weights.
Age/gender are collapsed secondary controls with truthful explanations, explicit enablement, and neutral missing/disabled behavior.
Settings clearly separates Personalization, Ranking, and Privacy & local data and does not duplicate full source administration.
Semantic ranking choices round-trip deterministically to the existing backend configuration, preserve caps, and do not destroy compatible custom saved values.
All non-obvious controls include useful examples/helper text and actionable field errors.
Profile/ranking/source choices remain same-origin and SQLite-authoritative across a full process restart.
verification: Add component tests for chip entry/removal/duplicates/keyboard use, step navigation, simplified location, optional disclosure, and validation.
Add exact mapping and round-trip tests for semantic presets, custom configurations, canonical defaults, and demographic caps.
Run the real-process onboarding workflow with Hungary/Budapest and optional demographics, then restart against the same SQLite database.
Run desktop/narrow screenshot, keyboard, accessibility, storage, and no-geolocation/network assertions.
non_goals: Per-interest numeric tuning in normal onboarding
tasks.handoff_notes: If the existing location or ranking contract truly cannot support the accepted UX, stop and request a separate contract task rather than silently changing backend files outside this task.

tasks.title: Redesign ranked feed, refresh feedback, article cards, and explanations
tasks.summary: Create the core consumer reading experience with compact refresh state, a coherent responsive filter bar, distinct article cards, balanced actions, and concise backend-driven explanations without raw floats.
tasks.objective: Make refresh, filtering, story boundaries, reading actions, and why-this-story reasons immediately understandable while preserving server order and authority.
tasks.context: The backend owns ranking order, contributions, filter persistence, library mutations, and permissions. The frontend may reorganize presentation but must not recompute or invent those results.
outputs: Ranked-feed header and compact refresh UI
Responsive filter bar with More filters
implementation_notes: Keep complete refresh outcomes recoverable and accessible, but collapse completed details behind a compact status/disclosure.
Bind every cursor to the successful applied filter snapshot and retain server-authoritative filter persistence/restart behavior.
Use source, publication time, title, excerpt, primary read/open action, and subordinate library actions in a consistent card hierarchy.
Render backend reason codes as concise truthful bullets. Hide raw contribution numbers by default; any debug values require a labeled advanced disclosure.
Preserve metadata-only/full-content behavior, outbound publisher clarity, mutation invalidation, stale/retry states, and route/unmount race protections.
acceptance_criteria: Refresh is a clear action near the feed heading; terminal success is compact and partial failure offers accessible details without dominating the page.
Filters form one coherent responsive bar/panel, More filters contains date/hidden options, and Clear filters appears only when active.
Articles are visually distinct keyboard-accessible cards with obvious story hierarchy and secondary actions that do not overpower reading.
Default explanations show human-readable production reasons and no long raw floating-point contribution values.
Server order, cursor stability, filter persistence, library invalidation, permission-aware reader behavior, and publisher fallback remain correct.
Initial, stale/retry, empty, loading-more, refresh-running/partial, and API-unavailable states remain distinct and accessible.
verification: Add component tests for compact refresh outcomes/details, filter active state/reflow, article actions, explanation disclosure, reason mapping, and hidden raw scores.
Retain and extend deferred-request tests for cursor/filter generations, route changes, mutation uncertainty, and component disposal.
Run real-process refresh-to-feed, explanation, reader/link-out, read/save/hide, API interruption, filter restart, and recovery coverage.
Capture desktop/narrow feed, expanded explanation, reader, empty/error, and partial-refresh evidence with keyboard/a11y checks.
tasks.handoff_notes: Consume UX-001 primitives. Do not broaden shared global styling or change backend reason/score semantics in this task.

tasks.title: Redesign Sources and Library workflows
tasks.summary: Apply the shared consumer design language to source configuration, manual refresh context, library views, forms, validation, empty states, and reversible actions.
tasks.objective: Make source identity, enabled/permission/policy state, expected custom values, and saved/read/hidden library workflows easy to scan and operate.
tasks.context: Source permissions, credentials, scraper policy, refresh outcomes, and library authority are already accepted and must not be weakened for visual convenience.
implementation_notes: Use clear source names, kinds, enabled states, permission modes, credential configured state, and scraper-policy status without exposing secrets or unnecessary protocol jargon.
Provide realistic URL/config examples and explain feed/API/content permission choices in plain language while preserving every authoritative validation.
Keep credential input write-only and clear it on all accepted lifecycle paths.
Use the same article cards/action hierarchy for Saved, Read, Unread, and Hidden views; preserve independent reversible states and hidden restoration ranking semantics.
Do not duplicate full source management in Settings or make refresh state inconsistent with the feed.
acceptance_criteria: Configured and starter sources are clearly separated and scannable, with obvious enabled, permission, adapter, credential, and policy state.
Every non-obvious source field has a useful example/helper and actionable error; a normal RSS setup does not require interpreting internal protocol models.
Credentials, metadata-only/full-content permission, approved scraper policy, and sanitized failures remain truthful and enforced.
Saved/read/unread/hidden Library views use consistent cards, empty/error states, filters, and reversible actions at desktop and narrow widths.
Source and library state remain authoritative after navigation, reload, mutation uncertainty, and full process restart.
verification: Update component tests for starter/configured cards, each source kind, helpers/errors, credential lifecycle, permission/policy states, refresh context, Library empty/error/action states, and mutation races.
Run sentinel checks across DOM, logs, snapshots, caches, and browser storage.
Run real-process source creation/refresh and saved/read/hidden/restore flows through restart.
Capture desktop/narrow Sources and Library evidence and run keyboard/accessibility/overflow checks.
tasks.handoff_notes: Consume UX-001 primitives and coordinate refresh presentation with UX-003 without editing its feed-owned files.

tasks.title: Integrate and visually verify the complete redesigned workflow
tasks.summary: Assemble the redesigned screens, resolve cross-screen inconsistencies, update the real-process workflow/evidence, and fix rendered desktop/narrow problems discovered outside isolated component tests.
tasks.objective: Deliver one coherent consumer application rather than individually improved screens with inconsistent transitions or visual behavior.
tasks.context: This sequential integration task begins only after onboarding/settings, feed/reader, and Sources/Library tasks are merged and independently approved.
outputs: Updated real-process E2E and evidence generation
implementation_notes: Inspect actual rendered output rather than trusting snapshots or tests; fix cross-screen spacing, grouping, focus, navigation, action, and responsive inconsistencies discovered during the complete workflow.
Use only fictional/permitted deterministic fixtures; do not introduce live external providers or outbound services.
Preserve API interruption/recovery, process restart, filter/profile/source/library persistence, browser-storage privacy, and loopback-only request audits.
Do not use this integration task for unrelated refactors, ranking changes, or new product features.
acceptance_criteria: A first-time user can immediately understand interests, optional Hungary/Budapest location, secondary demographics, source selection, and one Finish setup action.
Settings, feed, reader, Sources, and Library share consistent hierarchy, spacing, surfaces, controls, actions, status, empty/error states, and responsive behavior.
Normal UI contains no unexplained raw ranking weights or long raw contribution floats.
Refresh, filters, articles, explanations, read/save/hide/restore, source configuration, and recovery are clear at desktop and approximately 390px with no horizontal overflow.
Profile, ranking configuration, sources, library state, and server-backed filters survive a real Go-process restart on the same SQLite database.
Keyboard path, automated accessibility, browser-storage audit, loopback-only request audit, content permissions, credential secrecy, and Windows build remain passing.
verification: Run full repository verification, frontend lint/typecheck/tests/build, Go tests/race/vet, contract/drift checks, and Windows amd64 build.
Run the complete real-process E2E from empty data through setup, sources, mixed refresh, feed, explanation, reader/link-out, library actions, filters, API interruption, restart, and restored state.
Run automated accessibility at every core screen plus a meaningful keyboard-only path and narrow viewport assertions.
Audit browser storage and outbound requests and assert raw weights/long contribution floats are absent from normal UI.
Record screenshots for onboarding, Settings, feed, expanded explanation, Sources, Library, empty/error states, and narrow viewport.
tasks.handoff_notes: Submit exact-revision evidence to UX-VERIFY-001. Passing automation without the complete rendered screenshot set is insufficient.
